```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Prasanchaimontri_2024_favipiravir"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Prasanchaimontri_2024_favipiravir"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/prp2.1233> (open access; PMC11542727)

# Population

Prasanchaimontri 2024 is a pharmacokinetic sub-study nested in a prospective
randomized trial of favipiravir in Thai adults with symptomatic, PCR-confirmed
COVID-19 without pneumonia. Eight of the 62 patients in the favipiravir arm
took part: seven women and one man, median age 39 years (range 19-53) and
median BMI 27.9 kg/m^2 (18.0-33.6). The Supplementary Methods give a mean (SD)
weight of 67.9 (15.45) kg and BSA of 1.70 (0.19) m^2. All received 1800 mg
twice daily on day 1 and 800 mg twice daily thereafter: four patients for 14
days, three for 7 days, and one (Patient 2) stopped on day 4 because of a rash.
Plasma was sampled before and 1 h after the dose on days 1-5, 7 and 14.

The same information is available programmatically:

```{r population}
str(readModelDb("Prasanchaimontri_2024_favipiravir")()$population)
```

# Source trace

The paper used a two-stage approach. Each patient was fitted individually with
a one-compartment first-order-absorption model (R `pracma::lsqnonlin`,
1/predicted^2 weighting), and the population was summarised by statistics of
the eight individual estimates (Table 1). The packaged model carries those
summary statistics.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| One-compartment model, first-order absorption | n/a | Methods, 'Pharmacokinetic modeling and simulation' |
| `CL/F(day n) = CL/F(day 1) * (1 + Factor * (n - 1))` | n/a | Methods, equation 1 (image e001) |
| `lka` | log(3.4) 1/h | Table 1, 'Geometric mean' K_A |
| `lcl` | log(1.0) L/h | Table 1, 'Geometric mean' CL/F |
| `lvc` | log(19.5) L | Table 1, 'Geometric mean' V/F |
| `cl_time_slope` | 0.024 per day | Table 1, 'Arithmetic mean' daily % change in CL/F = 2.4 |
| `etalka` | 1.8 | Table 1, 'Variance of log-transformed parameter' K_A |
| `etalcl` | 0.3 | Table 1, 'Variance of log-transformed parameter' CL/F |
| `etalvc` | 0.1 | Table 1, 'Variance of log-transformed parameter' V/F |
| `propSd` | 0 (not reported) | Methods: 1/predicted^2 weighting, no magnitude given |

## Consistency of the Table 1 summary rows

The summary rows of Table 1 are recomputed below from the eight individual
estimates printed in the same table. The individual values are rounded to one
decimal, so small differences are expected.

```{r table1}
table1 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~patient, ~cl, ~vc, ~ka, ~daily_pct,
  1, 1.2, 22.8, 1.5, 10.6,
  2, 0.7, 13.5, 6.3, -7.8,
  3, 1.5, 24.9, 5.9, 6.3,
  4, 0.8, 14.7, 6.0, 8.1,
  5, 0.7, 14.1, 1.8, 9.5,
  6, 2.7, 38.0, 19.4, -3.8,
  7, 1.0, 17.8, 7.1, -7.2,
  8, 0.6, 19.1, 0.2, 3.5
)
recomputed <- tibble::tibble(
  statistic = c("Geometric mean", "Variance of log", "Arithmetic mean", "SD"),
  `CL/F (L/h)` = c(exp(mean(log(table1$cl))), var(log(table1$cl)), mean(table1$cl), sd(table1$cl)),
  `V/F (L)` = c(exp(mean(log(table1$vc))), var(log(table1$vc)), mean(table1$vc), sd(table1$vc)),
  `ka (1/h)` = c(exp(mean(log(table1$ka))), var(log(table1$ka)), mean(table1$ka), sd(table1$ka)),
  `Daily % change` = c(NA, NA, mean(table1$daily_pct), sd(table1$daily_pct))
)
knitr::kable(recomputed, digits = 2,
             caption = "Summary statistics recomputed from the individual estimates in Table 1.")
```

The recomputed geometric means (1.0 L/h, 19.5 L, 3.4 1/h), the daily-change
mean (2.4 %) and its SD (7.6 %) match the printed rows. The log-variances of
CL/F and V/F round to the printed 0.3 and 0.1. The ka log-variance recomputes
to about 1.95 against the printed 1.8: Patient 8's ka is printed as 0.2 1/h,
and at one decimal its log is uncertain by about 0.25. The printed 1.8 is
packaged.

```{r table1-check}
stopifnot(
  abs(exp(mean(log(table1$cl))) - 1.0) < 0.05,
  abs(exp(mean(log(table1$vc))) - 19.5) < 0.1,
  abs(exp(mean(log(table1$ka))) - 3.4) < 0.1,
  abs(mean(table1$daily_pct) - 2.4) < 0.05
)
```

# Replicate Figure 2: individual fits

Each patient's individual parameters (Table 1) are passed to the packaged
model with the random effects removed, using the nominal twice-daily regimen
and the treatment duration given in the Results. Observation times are not
published at the precision needed to overlay the measured points, so only the
fitted curves are shown.

```{r figure-2}
mod <- readModelDb("Prasanchaimontri_2024_favipiravir")
mod_typical <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)

# Doses every 12 h from time 0; 1800 mg on day 1, 800 mg after.
dose_days <- c(14, 3.5, 14, 14, 14, 7, 7, 7) # Patient 2 stopped on day 4
make_regimen <- function(id, n_days, loading, maintenance, t_end) {
  dose_time <- seq(0, by = 12, length.out = round(n_days * 2))
  doses <- tibble::tibble(
    id = id, time = dose_time, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot",
    amt = ifelse(dose_time < 24, loading, maintenance)
  )
  obs <- tibble::tibble(id = id, time = seq(0, t_end, by = 1), evid = 0L,
                        cmt = "central", amt = 0)
  dplyr::bind_rows(doses, obs) |> dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}

ev_ind <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(table1)), function(i) {
  make_regimen(i, dose_days[i], 1800, 800, t_end = dose_days[i] * 24 + 24)
}))

params_ind <- table1 |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    id = patient,
    lcl = log(cl), lvc = log(vc), lka = log(ka),
    cl_time_slope = daily_pct / 100
  )

sim_ind <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typical, events = ev_ind, params = params_ind,
                           returnType = "data.frame")

ggplot(dplyr::filter(sim_ind, time > 0), aes(time / 24, Cc)) +
  geom_line(colour = "steelblue") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 25, linetype = "dashed", colour = "red") +
  facet_wrap(~id, ncol = 4, labeller = label_both) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (days)", y = "Favipiravir plasma concentration (mg/L)",
       caption = "Replicates the fitted curves of Figure 2 of Prasanchaimontri 2024; dashed line = EC90 25 mg/L.")
```

The Results report that measured Cmin and Cmax ranged from 12.1 to 132.2 mg/L
and 14.5 to 201.2 mg/L across patients and days. The fitted curves span a
comparable range during dosing.

```{r figure-2-range}
# Restrict to the dosing period: from the second dose to each patient's last dose.
last_dose <- tibble::tibble(id = seq_along(dose_days), last_dose = (round(dose_days * 2) - 1) * 12)
sim_ind |>
  dplyr::left_join(last_dose, by = "id") |>
  dplyr::filter(time >= 12, time <= last_dose) |>
  dplyr::summarise("Lowest fitted Cc (mg/L)" = min(Cc), "Highest fitted Cc (mg/L)" = max(Cc)) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
```

# Virtual cohort and Figure 3

Figure 3 of the paper shows the 90 % prediction interval of 1000 simulated
profiles drawn from the Table 1 parameters. Panel A uses the Thai regimen
(1800/800 mg twice daily) and panel D the 1600/600 mg regimen used in the
Turkish study. Here 200 virtual patients per regimen are simulated over 15
days, with 14 days of twice-daily dosing.

```{r cohort}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20241107)
n_per_arm <- 200
regimens <- tibble::tibble(
  regimen = c("1800/800 mg BID", "1600/600 mg BID"),
  loading = c(1800, 1600),
  maintenance = c(800, 600)
)
obs_times <- seq(0, 360, by = 1)
ev_pop <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(regimens)), function(r) {
  ids <- (r - 1) * n_per_arm + seq_len(n_per_arm)
  dose_time <- seq(0, 324, by = 12)
  doses <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = dose_time) |>
    dplyr::mutate(evid = 1L, cmt = "depot",
                  amt = ifelse(time < 24, regimens$loading[r], regimens$maintenance[r]))
  obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = obs_times) |>
    dplyr::mutate(evid = 0L, cmt = "central", amt = 0)
  dplyr::bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    dplyr::mutate(regimen = regimens$regimen[r])
})) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))

sim_pop <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev_pop, keep = "regimen",
                           returnType = "data.frame")
```

```{r figure-3}
band <- sim_pop |>
  dplyr::group_by(regimen, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), Q50 = median(Cc), Q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(dplyr::filter(band, time > 0), aes(time / 24)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = pmax(Q05, 0.05), ymax = Q95), fill = "lightblue", alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_line(aes(y = Q50), colour = "steelblue") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 25, colour = "red") +
  facet_wrap(~regimen) +
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(0.05, 500)) +
  labs(x = "Time (days)", y = "Favipiravir plasma concentration (mg/L)",
       caption = paste("Replicates Figure 3A (1800/800 mg) and 3D (1600/600 mg) of",
                       "Prasanchaimontri 2024: median and 90% prediction interval."))
```

Read from Figure 3A, the published median is about 36 mg/L at the day-13
trough and about 6.5 mg/L at day 15, 36 h after the last dose. The simulated
medians are compared below.

```{r figure-3-check}
fig3a <- band |>
  dplyr::filter(regimen == "1800/800 mg BID", time %in% c(312, 360)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    timepoint = ifelse(time == 312, "Day 13 trough (312 h)", "Day 15 (360 h)"),
    published_median = ifelse(time == 312, 36, 6.5)
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(timepoint, published_median, simulated_median = Q50,
                simulated_Q05 = Q05, simulated_Q95 = Q95)
fig3a |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Time point" = timepoint,
    "Figure 3A median (mg/L, read from plot)" = published_median,
    "Simulated median (mg/L)" = simulated_median,
    "Simulated 5th percentile" = simulated_Q05,
    "Simulated 95th percentile" = simulated_Q95
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)

# Medians only: the tails of a 200-subject cohort are not reproducible across
# rxode2 builds, and the published values are read from a plot.
stopifnot(
  abs(fig3a$simulated_median[1] / 36 - 1) < 0.25,
  abs(fig3a$simulated_median[2] / 6.5 - 1) < 0.5
)
```

## Distribution of the daily change in CL/F

Table 1 summarises the daily change in CL/F only on the arithmetic scale, and
three of the eight individual values are negative, so the paper does not say
how it was distributed in the simulations. The chunk below draws one set of
CL/F, V/F and ka values in base R and pairs it with three readings of the
daily change: a normal distribution with the Table 1 SD, a log-normal
distribution moment-matched to the Table 1 mean and variance, and the fixed
mean that the packaged model uses.

```{r slope-readings}
set.seed(20241107)
n_alt <- 200
base_draw <- tibble::tibble(
  id = seq_len(n_alt),
  lcl = log(1.0) + rnorm(n_alt, 0, sqrt(0.3)),
  lvc = log(19.5) + rnorm(n_alt, 0, sqrt(0.1)),
  lka = log(3.4) + rnorm(n_alt, 0, sqrt(1.8))
)
slope_var <- 57.3 / 100^2 # Table 1 'Variance' of the daily % change, as a fraction
ln_sigma2 <- log(1 + slope_var / 0.024^2)
slope_draws <- list(
  "Normal, SD 7.6 %" = rnorm(n_alt, 0.024, sqrt(slope_var)),
  "Log-normal, moment-matched" = exp(rnorm(n_alt, log(0.024) - ln_sigma2 / 2, sqrt(ln_sigma2))),
  "Fixed 2.4 % (packaged)" = rep(0.024, n_alt)
)
ev_alt <- ev_pop |>
  dplyr::filter(regimen == "1800/800 mg BID") |>
  dplyr::select(-regimen)
alt <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(slope_draws), function(nm) {
  p <- dplyr::mutate(base_draw, cl_time_slope = slope_draws[[nm]])
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typical, events = ev_alt, params = p, returnType = "data.frame") |>
    dplyr::filter(time %in% c(312, 360)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(reading = nm)
}))
alt_summary <- alt |>
  dplyr::group_by(reading, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(median = median(Cc), q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95), .groups = "drop")
alt_summary |>
  dplyr::rename("Reading" = reading, "Time (h)" = time,
                "Median Cc (mg/L)" = median, "95th percentile Cc (mg/L)" = q95) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Figure 3A at the day-13 trough (312 h) and day 15 (360 h) under three readings of the daily change in CL/F.")

# Share of subjects whose CL/F reaches zero or below by day 14 under the
# normal reading: 1 + slope * 13 <= 0.
mean(1 + slope_draws[["Normal, SD 7.6 %"]] * 13 <= 0)
```

Figure 3A shows a day-15 upper bound of about 50 mg/L. Under the normal
reading, the subjects whose CL/F falls to zero accumulate drug, and the
95th percentile climbs far above that. The packaged fixed-mean reading
reproduces the published median line most closely.

```{r slope-readings-check}
q95_d15 <- setNames(
  alt_summary$q95[alt_summary$time == 360],
  alt_summary$reading[alt_summary$time == 360]
)
# The normal reading's upper tail is driven by CL/F reaching zero; it sits
# several-fold above the fixed-mean reading in any cohort of this size.
stopifnot(q95_d15[["Normal, SD 7.6 %"]] > 3 * q95_d15[["Fixed 2.4 % (packaged)"]])
```

# PKNCA validation

The paper does not report NCA parameters. PKNCA is run on the simulated
1800/800 mg and 1600/600 mg cohorts over the first dosing interval (0-12 h,
after the 1800 or 1600 mg loading dose) and over a day-13 interval (300-312 h)
to show the decline in exposure as CL/F rises by 2.4 % per day.

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim_pop |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, regimen)
sim_nca <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  sim_nca,
  sim_nca |> dplyr::distinct(id, regimen) |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, regimen, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, regimen, time)

dose_df <- ev_pop |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, regimen)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | regimen + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | regimen + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = c(0, 300), end = c(12, 312),
  cmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

nca_summary <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "cmin", "auclast")) |>
  dplyr::group_by(regimen, start, end, PPTESTCD) |>
  dplyr::summarise(median = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median)

nca_summary |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Regimen" = regimen, "Start (h)" = start, "End (h)" = end,
    "Median Cmax (mg/L)" = cmax, "Median Cmin (mg/L)" = cmin,
    "Median AUC0-12 (mg*h/L)" = auclast
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Simulated NCA by regimen and dosing interval.")
```

Over a 12-hour interval at steady state, AUC equals dose / (CL/F). The
day-13 median AUC for the 1800/800 mg regimen should therefore be near
800 / (1.0 * (1 + 0.024 * 12)) = 621 mg*h/L, less a few percent because
steady state is approached under a clearance that keeps rising.

```{r pknca-check}
auc_d13 <- nca_summary |>
  dplyr::filter(regimen == "1800/800 mg BID", start == 300) |>
  dplyr::pull(auclast)
expected_auc_d13 <- 800 / (1.0 * (1 + 0.024 * 12))
auc_d13 / expected_auc_d13
stopifnot(abs(auc_d13 / expected_auc_d13 - 1) < 0.15)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Two-stage summary as a population model.** The paper estimated no
  population parameters. Typical values are the Table 1 geometric means and the
  between-subject variances the variances of the log-transformed individual
  estimates, which is how the Methods describe the population simulations
  ("assuming log-normal distributions"). All are wrapped in `fixed()` to show
  that none was estimated as a population parameter.
* **No between-subject variability on the daily change in CL/F.** Table 1 gives
  the daily change only as an arithmetic mean (2.4 %) and variance (57.3,
  SD 7.6 %); no log-scale summary is possible because three of the eight
  individual values are negative. The section "Distribution of the daily
  change in CL/F" compares three readings against Figure 3A. A normal
  distribution with SD 7.6 % sends CL/F to zero or below by day 14 in about
  one subject in ten and pushes the 95th percentile far above the published
  interval, so the authors cannot have simulated it. A log-normal distribution
  moment-matched to the arithmetic mean and variance raises the day-15 median
  above the published line. A fixed 2.4 % per day reproduces the published
  median (about 36 mg/L at the day-13 trough and 6.5 mg/L at day 15), so that
  reading is packaged. Users who want the observed spread can add an
  additive eta on `cl_time_slope` with variance 0.00573, keeping in mind that
  it allows CL/F to become non-positive in long simulations.
* **Dosing-day index.** The equation's day number `n` is taken as the day
  counted from the first dose at time 0 (`floor(t / 24) + 1`), so CL/F steps up
  once every 24 h. The paper does not say whether the change continues after
  dosing stops; the model continues it, which affects only the washout tail.
* **Residual error.** The fits used 1/predicted^2 weighting (proportional
  error) but no magnitude was reported, so `propSd` is fixed at 0.
* **ka.** The individual ka estimates are imprecise (RSE up to 14982 %), which
  drives the large log-variance (1.8). The abstract quotes a mean ka of
  "6.1 h"; Table 1 gives an arithmetic mean of 6.0 1/h and the Results text
  6.1 1/h. The geometric mean (3.4 1/h) is packaged.
* **Metabolite.** T-705M1 was measured but not modelled.
* No erratum was found for this article (Europe PMC search, 2026-10-31).
